discovery.none: Deliberate. Nothing in the advertisement names a EUC: the BLE serial module each brand fits is generic and its transport characteristic UUID is module-specific (WheelLog reads it from the connected wheel rather than restating one), and the brand itself is only learned from the first notification packets — King Song's AA 55 header, Gotway's 55 AA with the 5A5A5A5A footer, Veteran's DC 5A 5C. That evidence arrives after a connection, which is a scan's output and not its input, so an advertisement axis written from it would claim wheels this spec cannot decode and miss the ones it can. Manual selection until a discriminating advertisement turns up.

device.name: Electric Unicycles (King Song / Gotway-Begode / Veteran) — WheelLog
device.notes:
Electric unicycles from King Song, Gotway/Begode and Veteran/Leaperkim are decoded by the open-source WheelLog Android app. Each brand is a notify-stream of fixed-length framed packets over a BLE serial characteristic; brand is identified from the first packets rather than a fixed advertised UUID. Fully local BLE, no cloud. The per-brand frame formats below are the load-bearing facts; the transport characteristic UUID is device-specific (obtain it from the connected wheel / WheelLog).
KING SONG (KingsongAdapter): 20-byte frame, header AA 55, trailer 14 5A 5A; the packet-type selector is byte 16. Live-data type 0xA9: voltage bytes 2-3 (LE), speed 4-5, total distance 6-9 (32-bit), current 10-11, temperature 12-13. Other types: 0xB9 distance/time/fan, 0xBB name/model, 0xB3 serial, 0xA4/0xB5 speed/alarm settings, 0xF1/0xF2 dual-battery BMS. Commands (write byte 16): beep 0x88, request name 0x9B, request serial 0x63, power-off 0x40.
GOTWAY / BEGODE (GotwayAdapter): 24-byte frame, header 55 AA, footer 5A 5A 5A 5A (bytes 20-23); type byte at index 18 — 0x00 live "Frame A", 0x04 "Frame B" (totals/settings), 0x07 motor-temp/batt-current, 0x01/0x02/0x03 BMS, 0xFF advanced settings. Frame A (big-endian): voltage 2-3 (1/100 V), speed 4-5 (km/h = x3.6), distance 8-9 (m), phase current 10-11 (1/100 A signed), temperature 12-13 (v/340 + 36.53 C), PWM 14-15. Voltage base 67.2 V with a config-selected multiplier (0->1.0x ... 4->2.0x) to cover 84/100.8 V packs. Commands (ASCII): beep 'b', calibration 'c', lights E/Q/T, max-speed 'W', miles/km 'm'/'g'.
VETERAN / LEAPERKIM (VeteranAdapter): header DC 5A 5C + length byte; big-endian: voltage @4, speed @6 (x10 signed), distance @8 (word-reversed int), total distance @12, phase current @16 (x10), temperature @18; CRC32 on longer frames. 24S (100.8 V nominal) reference.
SAFETY: beep/lights/max-speed/calibration commands are unauthenticated by design in these decoders.

openness.notes: No vendor documentation; WheelLog reverse-engineered each brand's frames. The BLE transport characteristic UUID lives in WheelLog's BLE service class (not the per-brand adapters) and is not restated here.

credentials.notes: No pairing/auth documented; frames are unauthenticated over BLE. No Wi-Fi.
stored_on_device: Per-brand wheel settings (speed limits, alarms, lights)

factory_reset.effect: No documented BLE factory reset; per-brand settings are command writes, not a single reset. Not transcribed here.

methods.description: Connect over BLE, subscribe to the wheel's serial/notify characteristic, and decode the incoming frames per the brand detected from the header.

steps.action: Connect and subscribe to the wheel's BLE serial characteristic.
Detect the brand from the first packets and decode live data per the frame format.

setup.notes: Connect to the wheel's BLE serial characteristic and subscribe to notifications; the brand is auto-detected from the first packets. No pairing secret. Confidence medium: King Song and Gotway frames are fully read from the adapters; Veteran offsets are read but less cross-checked.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The per-brand frame formats (headers, field offsets, command bytes) are from WheelLog's Android per-brand adapters. NOTE: the BLE serial characteristic UUID is module/brand-specific and was not captured from a cited source, so it is not asserted here — WheelLog auto-detects the brand from the first packets.
